page: Microsoft Azure F80alds_v7 belongs to the compute-optimized Faldsv7 family, operating on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. It provisions 80 dedicated physical cores powered by AMD EPYC 9V45 processors based on the x86_64 architecture, reaching clock speeds of 4.5 GHz. The CPU architecture allocates one thread per physical core, avoiding simultaneous multithreading overhead and ensuring predictable processing throughput. Hardware instruction support is extensive, featuring AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16 alongside accelerated cryptography via VAES and SHA-NI. The instance is configured with 160 GB of system memory, matching a standard compute-optimized ratio of 2 GB per vCPU, and is bundled with 9449 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark evaluations place the F80alds_v7 in the top tier for multi-core compute, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 290383.74 and a PassMark CPU score of 128198.66. Memory subsystems demonstrate strong throughput, exceeding 477 GB/sec in large-block read operations, which complements the high processing rate. The platform also registers high scores in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput at 114.32 GB/sec. However, the memory allocation of 2 GB per core represents a clear tradeoff for memory-bound software, limiting its suitability for massive in-memory datasets despite the high processor core density.

From a resource efficiency perspective, bundling 9.4 TB of high-speed local NVMe storage with 80 physical execution cores offers strong qualitative value for pipelines requiring fast local scratch space without auxiliary storage attachments. The dedicated single-thread-per-core layout avoids shared-core resource contention. Workloads well matched to this profile include software compilation pipelines, numerical simulation modeling, static web serving at scale, ETL batch processing, and medium-scale LLM prompt evaluation.
description: Microsoft Azure F80alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine equipped with 80 dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor cores running at 4.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. With one physical core per vCPU, it eliminates hyperthreading contention across multi-threaded operations. Memory capacity is provisioned at 160 GB, reflecting a compute-centric 2 GB per core ratio. The instance includes 9449 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage, providing high-throughput local scratch space without relying solely on remote volumes. In benchmark testing, the F80alds_v7 achieves top-tier results in single- and multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU ratings, memory bandwidth, and compression. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU profile makes it less suited for massive in-memory databases, but highly cost-efficient for core-bound tasks that benefit from dedicated physical compute alongside substantial fast scratch storage. It delivers an effective hardware balance for compute workloads including continuous integration, numerical simulations, static web serving, and distributed batch processing.
